info.title: Catalog API
info.description:
The backend of the Catalog Android app: accounts, contacts, messages released later (on a date, an occasion or after inactivity), the recipient link, the inactivity switch and its trusted contact.

Every JSON response is wrapped in one envelope: `{"status_code": int, "data": <payload or null>, "error": null or {"message", "code", "details"?}}`. The schemas below show it. Authenticated endpoints take `Authorization: Bearer <access>`.

The written guide, with error codes, rate limits and flows, is `docs/API.md` in the backend repository.

post.description:
POST /api/v1/admin/control/deliveries/<id>/retry

Sends a `failed` or `queued` e-mail delivery of a live message again, now.
In one transaction the delivery gets a fresh link token (never returned)
and goes back to `queued`, and the audit entry is written; the e-mail goes
out once that commits, through the same after-commit path a release uses
(attempts + 1, then `sent` or `failed`). The response is the delivery
after that send: a send that fails is a 200 with status `failed` and the
new `last_error`.

This is an explicit human override, so it is not bound by the automatic
five-attempt cap (MAX_EMAIL_ATTEMPTS): it may run past it, and still
counts the attempt. Anything else (in-app, already sent, deleted message,
a contact with no address) is 400 `invalid_state`. Audited as
DELIVERY_RETRIED.

while any live user is on the plan.

get.description:
GET /api/v1/admin/control/stats/overview

Definitions:
- users.total / new_7d / verified count accounts that are not soft-deleted;
  `suspended` is status=suspended among them; `deleted` counts soft-deleted ones.
- messages: live (not soft-deleted) messages per status.
- deliveries_24h: the last 24 hours, by status. sent, delivered and opened
  are counted by `sent_at`; failed and queued by `updated_at` (they have no
  send time, and updated_at is when they last changed).
- switches: enabled-or-not inactivity switches per state, plus `enabled`.
- trustee_pending: trustee confirmations still awaiting a decision.
- tickets_open: support tickets not yet resolved or closed.
- leads_new: business leads with status new.

post.description:
Soft-deletes an account.

Nothing is removed: the row and everything that points at it survive,
because deleting them would tear holes in related records. We
stamp `deleted_at` and clear `is_active`, which is what
actually revokes access — the login backend and SimpleJWT both refuse
inactive users, so any token already issued stops working immediately.

post.description: Always the same 200, whether or not a code went out. A code is sent only for `verify_email` to an unverified account, `reset_password` to an account that can sign in, and `recipient_access` to an email with a released message. Codes are 6 digits and expire after `expires_in_seconds`; a new code replaces the previous one.

post.description: `verify_email`: marks the email verified (this links contacts to the account, so messages reach the in-app inbox). `reset_password`: spends the code and returns `reset_token`. `recipient_access`: checks the code without spending it; /r/{token}/verify spends it. Every wrong guess counts; 5 spend the code.

actor_display.description:
Falls back to the stored label so a row still names who acted after the
account itself is gone — which is exactly when an audit trail earns its
keep.

actor_email.description:
The real email column, kept separate from actor_label: the label is
frozen at the time of the event, so it cannot be trusted as the
account's current address the way this field can. Empty once the account is
gone — an email nobody can look up is not useful, only actor_label's
frozen-at-the-time text is.
